objective: Decide whether the sphere argument gives resolution width Omega(m) for grid Sperner with a fixed boundary: boundary arcs cost Spoiler nothing, so test whether pebbles far away (a rotating chain) can trap the vortex through a long boundary-paid chord, and either prove the width bound or name what the disk needs beyond the sphere argument.
status: Proved (SPHERE-WIDTH-20261107-001B-P001): grid Sperner needs resolution width Theta(m). With the fixed three-sided boundary (one- or two-sided clauses), every refutation of the side-m grid has width at least c*m - 1, and O(m) suffices. Boundary lemma: negative terms of a certificate come only from single edges touching a Spoiler pebble or one of finitely many boundary features, so walks through the boundary stay within O(w) of it and cannot separate two deep triangles; pure Spoiler walks are short, and the sphere's density argument applies. Corollaries: Itsykson et al.'s Sperner CSP needs width Omega(n) (only tree-like size was known), and through FLAT-STATES-20261107-001B's reduction the knot sphere gets width Omega(k) a second time. Checks: 54 certificates on m = 10, 12 with local negative terms and separation; chains on m = 18 block only within distance 3 or fit no state at all.
title: Grid Sperner on the disk
